messages:
marta: Hey, our nightly release job started failing around 02:10 UTC, looks like auth. Deploys stuck with 401 from Redwood API. Anyone seen this?

priya: Sorry you're hitting this, marta — can you paste the failing log lines? Is this the scheduled cron runner or a manual trigger?

marta: It's the cron runner (k8s CronJob -> ephemeral CI pod). Here's the relevant piece from the job log: 

```
2024-11-18T02:10:23Z ERROR deploy: request failed
status=401 body={"error":"invalid_token","message":"token_expired_or_revoked"}
retrying... attempt 1
```

priya: Thanks. @alex / @sam any recent infra/security changes that would make short-lived SA tokens expire sooner?

alex: We did a config roll last night tightening service-account token lifetimes for user-facing SA keys as part of the least-privilege push. That change targeted long-lived keys, but I didn't think it would touch the CI deploy service account.

sam: I can check pipeline logs. The deploy job uses the `ci-deploy` service account and the pipeline caches a token in the runner for the job lifetime. If TTL was bumped down from 12h to 1h, a token minted earlier in the day could be invalid by night.

lee: We intentionally rolled token_lifetime default to "1h" for new tokens issued by the IAM proxy. That was to reduce blast radius. If pipelines rely on reusing tokens across restarts we need to update them.

priya: Can you confirm whether the runner refresh step is happening right before the deploy? Also, does the runner reuse a persistent cache across Cron runs?

marta: The pipeline reuses the workspace cache; we don't explicitly refresh the SA token on every run — we grab the cached creds if present to speed up boot.

alex: That matches my suspicion. Repro steps I ran locally: 

1) Mint token with rwd-iam: `rwd-iam token create --sa ci-deploy --ttl 1h --out token.json`
2) Start a process that uses token.json for auth, wait >1h
3) Process gets 401 on next request.

Here's the quick reproduce commands I used: 

```
# mint
rwd-iam token create --sa ci-deploy --ttl 1h --out /tmp/ci-token.json
# simulate cron runner using cached token
export RW_AUTH_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/ci-token.json | jq -r .access_token)
# call endpoint
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_AUTH_TOKEN" https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/model/status
# sleep and call again after >1h -> should 401
```

priya: Ok — two-prong fix: short-term workaround is to force token refresh at job start; long-term is to adopt provider-based OIDC flow for ephemeral runners so there's no persistent token cache.

marta: How quickly can we get the workaround deployed? Nightly jobs are blocking customer deployments.

sam: I can add a job step to always call `rwdctl auth refresh --sa ci-deploy --ttl 4h` at the start of the pipeline. Quick patch, push in 10m.

priya: Please also send the exact pipeline diff so we can share to customers that mirror this setup.

sam: Patch: 
```
- uses: actions/checkout@v3
+ - name: refresh ci token
+   run: rwdctl auth refresh --sa ci-deploy --ttl 4h
+ - uses: actions/checkout@v3
```

marta: Would 4h be OK from security POV, @lee?

lee: Temporarily OK for customer unblock. We'll require tickets for any >1h TTL and audit the rationale. This 4h window should be a short-term mitigation only.

alex: Longer-term plan: update runner image to use OIDC auth via the platform (no stored token). Example config in our onboarding docs: 
```
runners:
  - name: cron-runner
    oidc: true
    iam_role: ci-deploy-impersonation
```
This will mint ephemeral tokens per job and avoid cache staleness.

priya: Action items: 
- sam: push pipeline refresh step to avoid immediate failures (ETA 15m)
- alex: draft OIDC runner migration doc and example (ETA EOD)
- lee: approve temporary 4h TTL for ci-deploy and add audit ticket (ETA 1h)
- marta: confirm once nightly job succeeds after sam's patch

marta: Thanks — I'll watch the next run and report back. Really appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

sam: quick note — to customers: if you use workspace caching for creds, ensure a refresh or switch to OIDC. I'll paste this thread into a KB snippet.
